page: Amazon Web Services c6g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 12132.72 and single-core scoring 1519.38. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached reads at 472.95 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads and writes reach 124.9 GB/sec and 54.49 GB/sec, respectively. The instance exhibits average performance in software compilation with a score of 8600.0, ray tracing at 7099.0, and static web serving throughput at 9.46 GB/sec. However, it demonstrates weaker performance in single-threaded compression tasks, text processing, and LLM text generation, where it achieves 40.33 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 6.77 tokens/sec on a 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based Graviton architecture offers a specialized hardware profile that delivers balanced compute-to-memory resources without the overhead of local storage or GPU accelerators. The c6g.2xlarge is suited for multi-threaded compute workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and moderate image processing. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, high-throughput cryptographic operations, or large-scale LLM inference tasks.
